clue.text: Saying "ta", for example, by which to thwart going round

definitions.text: Saying "ta", for example, by which to thwart going round

indicators.note: the word for thwart is wrapped around the other letters, so it goes round them

parts.note: to balk is to thwart or obstruct
taken as written
taken as written: the toddler's word for thank you

explanation.surface: A remark about the word 'ta' and how it can head off trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: BALK, 'thwart', is the American-leaning spelling of baulk. The whole clue also describes the answer: 'ta' is the British nursery word for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Infant speech is full of shortened words like 'ta', the British child's thank you.

clue.text: Your leader, after his kind, is drunk

parts.note: a brand is a kind or type

indicators.note: the first letter of 'Your' leads it

explanation.surface: Your leader, behaving like the rest of his sort, is drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts Y after BRAND. In this puzzle 'drunk' defines a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit distilled from wine is something that gets drunk.

clue.text: Sailors from Somerset, soluble and scented

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset
salts are sailors, from old salt

explanation.surface: Sailors from a Somerset town are fragrant and dissolve.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is an English county in the south-west; BATH is its famous spa city. 'from' places BATH first.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystals added to a tub of water dissolve and give it perfume.

clue.text: A ferret who swore dreadfully, being drunk

indicators.note: dreadfully says the letters are badly treated and rearranged

explanation.surface: A ferret that cursed terribly while intoxicated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone in a poor state, such as intoxicated.

clue.text: The queen being partly in place, the king gets drunk

indicators.note: part of the queen's letters is put inside the word for place
part of the queen's letters is put inside the word for place

parts.note: lieu means place, as in 'in lieu of'

indicators.note: only part of the word queen is used, its opening

parts.note: R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: With the queen partly in his place, the king gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' takes the first two letters of 'queen', and 'being in' places them after the first two letters of the word for place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet flavoured spirit is something that gets drunk.

clue.text: Some honey at the battle?

parts.note: honey can come in a comb, so some honey is a comb
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about honey turning up at a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Fighting between forces is a synonym for a battle.

clue.text: The 9 is drunk

explanation.surface: A number nine is said to be drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: One more than eight is nine. The idiom means having had one drink too many.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine is literally one beyond eight; the idiom means slightly inebriated.

clue.text: It's sure to be the limit

explanation.surface: A remark that something is certain to be the outer boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Certain, as in bound to happen, is one sense; a boundary or edge is the other.

clue.text: Tyler, in the light, is drunk but not bottled

indicators.note: the rebel's name is placed inside the word for the light

parts.note: a taper is a thin candle, a light
Wat Tyler led the 1381 Peasants' Revolt

explanation.surface: A man called Tyler, under the lights, is drunk but not stoppered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links. Wat Tyler was the English rebel leader of 1381, so 'Tyler' gives WAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from the mains is drunk without coming in a bottle.

clue.text: African acquaintance's refusal coming up

parts.note: ken is knowledge or acquaintance

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up reads the word for refusal upwards

parts.note: nay is a refusal

explanation.surface: An African friend's refusal comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Nairobi's country is a native of Africa.

clue.text: Creative skill, that's for Shaw

parts.note: art is creative skill
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: Praise for an artistic talent belonging to the playwright Shaw.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests George Bernard Shaw, but the Shaw meant is Artie Shaw, the American swing bandleader and clarinettist.
explanation.definitionFit: The jazz clarinettist Shaw had the first name given here.

clue.text: To break into the line could sound huge in some company

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'To break into the line could sound huge in some company' (5-4): the definition is 'To break into the line', but no reading of 'could sound huge in some company' yields the letters of the answer without stretching.
annotationWithheld.clue: To break into the line could sound huge in some company

clue.text: Record party, a real find

parts.note: a disco is a party where records are played
very can mean real or genuine, as in 'the very thing'

explanation.surface: Someone at a record party makes a genuine find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a real find' reads as one phrase, but 'real' is VERY in its old sense of true or genuine, leaving 'find' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found, especially something valuable.

clue.text: A king at party opposed to return is drunk

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces is read backwards, as if returned

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a do is a party
v, short for versus, means opposed to

explanation.surface: A king at a party who is against going back gets drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to return' reverses AKDOV to VODKA. In this puzzle 'drunk' repeatedly defines a drink, something that is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Russian spirit is something that gets drunk.

clue.text: Caught unsuccessful person approaching?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a loser is someone who fails

explanation.surface: Someone who failed and got caught as the police drew near.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nearer is coming towards you, in the comparative.

clue.text: Managed reverse speed and tell the tale

indicators.note: the word for managed is turned backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a shop
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A driver who reversed at speed now has a story to tell.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount a story is to tell it.

clue.text: Melody, partial guide to pitch on imaginary instrument

parts.note: an air is a melody

indicators.note: only part of the word guide is used

parts.note: tar is pitch

explanation.surface: A melody, a partial guide to pitch, on an imaginary instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimed strumming of a non-existent six-string is an imaginary instrument.

clue.text: Card game when setter's two parts drunk?

parts.note: gin is one spirit that is drunk
rum is a second spirit that is drunk
my is what the setter says for belonging to the setter

explanation.surface: A card game played when the setter has had a couple of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummy variant for two players is a card game.

clue.text: Approaching to this point, as follows

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held 'Approaching to this point, as follows' (7): SO FAR is 'to this point', but no clue word fairly gives IN, and 'Approaching' and 'as follows' cannot both be placed without one doing two jobs; likely OCR damage.
annotationWithheld.clue: Approaching to this point, as follows

clue.text: The shabby get teased

explanation.surface: Poorly dressed people are mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattered or worn is one sense; mocked or ribbed is the other.

clue.text: Roman soldiers of a company that has some gardening

parts.note: hort, short for horticulture, is a part of the word for gardening

explanation.surface: A firm whose business includes some gardening.
explanation.walkthrough: HORT is the standard abbreviation for horticulture, the formal word for gardening.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman legion was divided into ten such units of soldiers.

clue.text: Nearly all the following proposition is blooming

definitions.note: an adjective here for the petal ring of a flower, a noun

indicators.note: nearly all means the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: a corollary is a proposition that follows from another

explanation.surface: Almost all of the next proposition is flourishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring of petals is the showy part of a flower in bloom.

clue.text: Why is the king going inside to get drunk?

indicators.note: the letters of is and king go into the word why

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Asking why the king is going indoors to get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks a question; the parse reads 'Why' as a word to be filled, not as a question word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch spirit is something that gets drunk.

clue.text: Additional comment is mounted

explanation.surface: Someone adds a remark while sitting on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause added to a document is one sense; a person on horseback is the other.

clue.text: On the way out of Normandy in good order

indicators.note: the letters come out of the run of words, in good order

explanation.surface: Something in Normandy is dying, but neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'normanDY IN Good'; 'in good order' says the letters are in sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the way out is near death.

clue.text: Today's candidates hold pole with yellow flowers

definitions.note: a plural phrase for the shrub that bears them

indicators.note: the first candidate's name holds the pole letter inside it

parts.note: Al Gore and George W. Bush, rivals in the 2000 US presidential election
S stands for the south pole
the second rival in that 2000 US election

explanation.surface: This year's election contenders grip a pole decorated with yellow blooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' puts S inside GORE. 'Today's' dates the clue: it appeared during the 2000 Gore versus Bush race.
explanation.definitionFit: Furze is a spiny shrub that bears bright yellow blossom.

clue.text: One in the labyrinth to lunch of polenta?

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed inside the word for the labyrinth

parts.note: a maze is a labyrinth
I is the Roman numeral one
lunch is a meal

explanation.surface: Someone lost in a labyrinth asks whether lunch will be polenta.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian cornmeal porridge is made from ground corn flour.

clue.text: Entrees to being a rich man

explanation.surface: Entry is the route to becoming wealthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrances or ways in are one sense; Bill, the very wealthy Microsoft founder, is the other.

clue.text: Solver's right to eat string for a dairy product

indicators.note: the solver's word swallows the string letter

parts.note: you is the solver, the person addressed
a G-string supplies the letter G

explanation.surface: The solver is entitled to eat some string to make a dairy food.
explanation.walkthrough: The G-string convention lets 'string' give the single letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented milk is a dairy food.

clue.text: Skilful setter's holding a flower on-line

indicators.note: the setter's word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: my is what the setter would say for belonging to the setter
an aster is a flower

explanation.surface: A skilful setter keeps a flower in an online picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'on-line' just joins the flower to its line in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing great skill is the mark of an expert craftsman.
